title: THE GOD WHO BRINGS US OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "God brought them out of Egypt; they have the strength of a wild ox. There is no divination against Jacob, no evil omens against Israel. It will now be said of Jacob and of Israel, 'See what God has done!'" - Num 23:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam points back to the great rescue: God brought Israel out of Egypt. This was the defining act of their history, the moment God displayed His power to save. And because of it, no divination or evil omen could prevail against them. The schemes of sorcerers were useless against a people God had redeemed.

The oracle rises to a triumphant note: it will be said of Israel, "See what God has done!" Their story was not a tale of their own greatness but a testimony to God's mighty acts. The nations would look at Israel and marvel, not at the people, but at their God. All the glory belonged to Him.

This reminds us that our salvation is God's work, not our own. Just as Israel could not have freed themselves from Egypt, we cannot free ourselves from sin. It is God who rescues, God who redeems, God who does what we could never do. Our story, too, becomes a display of His grace.

The exodus from Egypt points forward to the greater rescue accomplished by Christ, who brings us out of slavery to sin into the freedom of God's children (Rom 6:18). When people look at a redeemed life, may they say, "See what God has done!" Give Him the glory for the rescue only He could accomplish.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you recognise your salvation as entirely God's work?
2. When people look at your life, do they see what God has done?
3. How does the exodus point you to the greater rescue in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Redeeming God, thank You for the rescue only You could accomplish, bringing me out of slavery to sin through Christ. May my life declare to others, "See what God has done!" Amen.
